# Data Ownership

## Definition

Data Ownership is the assignment of accountability for a defined set of data — its meaning, quality, access and lifecycle — to a business role with the authority to make decisions about it.

## Explanation

Ownership is **accountability**, not possession or technical administration. The owning role ([[Data Owner]]) decides; [[Data Stewardship|stewardship]] executes day-to-day care; the [[Data Custodian]] operates the technical environment.

Ownership must be scoped: a data domain, a data set, a [[Business Concept|concept]] or a data product.

## Distinctions

- Ownership ≠ custody: IT operating a database does not own the data.
- Ownership ≠ authorship: the system or team creating data is not automatically its owner.

## Examples

- The head of Claims owns claims data, including approval of the definition of "Open Claim".
